uses: Young nettle tops are a traditional spring green, cooked into soups and puddings once the sting is gone, and Culpeper saw them as clearing out the heaviness of winter. In folk practice nettle tea was a spring tonic, a remedy for gout and aching joints, and a drink for new mothers. The herb was used to increase urine and flush the bladder, and a lotion of it was combed into the scalp for thinning hair. The tough stems were once spun into cloth and cord, and cottagers brewed nettle beer.
energetics: Culpeper called nettles somewhat hot, though not very hot
caution_pregnancy: Safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established, and the EMA does not recommend nettle leaf or herb then. Not enough is known; avoid medicinal amounts. Nettle is traditionally taken after birth and is said to help milk flow, with little evidence for that. Don't apply nettle to the breast while nursing: a baby got an allergic rash after its mother put nettle water on her nipples.
caution_medications: Because nettle makes you pass more urine, it may in theory add to the effects of diuretics (water pills). Animal studies suggest it may add to blood pressure medicines and may change how the body handles drugs broken down by liver CYP450 enzymes. How much any of this matters in people isn't known. Nettle may also lower blood sugar, so if you take diabetes medicines, ask your prescriber and watch for lows.
caution_conditions: Avoid it if you have been told to limit fluids, for example with serious heart or kidney disease, because it makes you pass more urine. See a doctor if urinary symptoms bring fever, pain, cramping or blood, or if a joint is swollen, red or feverish. Use isn't established for children under 12, and many nettle products aren't recommended under 18. Don't use it if you are allergic to nettle. Side effects can include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, heartburn, bloating and itchy rashes or hives. Rare case reports link nettle tea to breast swelling in a man and nipple discharge in a woman, and a nettle-containing remedy to low blood sugar in an older man.
caution_duration: If urinary or joint symptoms last more than 2 weeks, or get worse, see a doctor or qualified practitioner. The EMA allows long-term use of nettle root for prostate symptoms only after a doctor has ruled out serious disease.
caution_topical: Fresh leaves and stems sting with an intense burning itch that lasts minutes; cooking, drying or wilting removes the sting. Wear gloves to harvest, and keep young children away from the fresh plants. Hives and allergic rashes have been reported, and nettle pollen can trigger hay fever.
garden_harvest_timing: Gather young tops in spring, a few inches tall, with gloves. For drying, cut the plant before it flowers on a dry morning; avoid old autumn leaves, which turn gritty.
garden_water: Moist, rich soil; does poorly in drought
notes: Spreads by rhizomes and seed into dense patches and is treated as a weed in some places, so give it a corner of its own. It feeds the caterpillars of red admiral, painted lady and comma butterflies. Grieve records rubbing a sting with a dock leaf while saying a charm, and nettle linen woven in Scotland.
